title: Two-beat bass and the use of the bow
summary: Russell asks how early bassists played; Braud says two beats and more bow, which modern players neglect.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: In the old days, before you, when you were just a kid and heard the first bass players, how many beats in a major did they play? Did they play something like that? Two beats.

Two beats. Two beats. And more of the bow. The bow is very eccentric in some places. Now, the bass players of today, they don't use a bow. They don't know what it's for. See what I mean? And the bass comes in, plays a very big part on the string bass, in places you can use it. You know what I mean? Yeah. Some places you can use it like anything else, but it's knowing where to use it.
